goals: Mechanistic: contrast water partitioning (ET, surface runoff, subsurface drainage/recharge, snow storage) between a wet year (1993) and a dry year (2002) across the basin's elevation/soil heterogeneity.
Validation: compare simulated water output against in-domain observations where they exist (USGS gauges).

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM resolves the full water balance per point; the wet/dry contrast is a pure forcing-period swap (both years in NLDAS 1980-2018), and elevation/soil heterogeneity is captured by placing stratified columns.

answerable: Wet-year vs dry-year partitioning contrast at each column (ET / runoff / drainage / snow) — direct forcing-period swap.
Soil-texture control on partitioning within each year.
Coarse elevation gradient in partitioning and snow, as expressed through NLDAS 12 km orographic forcing differences and simulated SWE.

not_answerable.aspect: Quantitative validation against USGS stream gauges
not_answerable.why: Single-column ELM has no lateral routing; there is no native integrated streamflow to compare to a gauge without an aggregation/routing step the stack lacks.

not_answerable.aspect: Sub-12 km / ridgetop elevation-resolved snow and precip
not_answerable.why: NLDAS-2 is 0.125 deg (~12 km) with no within-cell lapse rate; high-relief detail and ridgetop SWE are unresolved/underestimated.
SNOTEL is sparse/missing in this basin per the brief; no co-located snow observations to validate against.

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation band x dominant soil), forcing-period swap applied to every column
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 elevation bands x 2 dominant soils = 6 base cells to span the heterogeneity, +2 replicate columns in the rain-snow transition band where wet/dry partitioning and snow-vs-rain response are most sensitive. Each column is run for BOTH 1993 and 2002, so the contrast is within-column (paired), keeping N small and interpretable.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate columns in the mid-elevation rain-snow transition (where the wet/dry partitioning difference is largest) and include valley-bottom low-elevation and high-elevation snow-dominated end members; let the expander pick real DEM/SSURGO points inside each band.
sampling_strategy.replication: 2 extra columns in the rain-snow transition band to capture within-band soil/aspect variability of the most sensitive process.

sampling_plan.reason: Valley-bottom end member: high-ET, runoff-limited response; baseline for the dry end of the water balance.
Tests soil-texture control on runoff vs infiltration at low elevation under both years.
Most sensitive band: isolates wet/dry partitioning shift and rain-vs-snow behavior on well-drained soil; replicated for within-band variability.
Same sensitive band on finer soil to separate soil from elevation effect on partitioning; replicated.
Snow-dominated end member: captures SWE storage and melt-driven drainage differences between wet and dry years.
High-elevation soil contrast on snowmelt partitioning into recharge vs runoff.

validation_design.comparison: aggregated — would require summing/routing column runoff to a gauge's contributing area; NOT possible as posed because the stack has no routing. Flagged as a gap, not a claimed validation.
validation_design.metric: annual/monthly runoff bias, wet-vs-dry ratio (if routing is added)
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on how many gauges the HUC contains and on routing availability

validation_design.comparison: analog only — SNOTEL is sparse/missing in-domain; any comparison would be an out-of-basin analog process check, not co-located validation.

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: forcing-period swap: wet year 1993 vs dry year 2002, native SSURGO soil per column, WTD-informed warm start + spin-up years before each analysis year

requires_capabilities.why: Convert independent 1-D column runoff into integrated streamflow at a contributing area.
requires_capabilities.blocks: Quantitative comparison to USGS gauges (the only in-domain observation).

requires_capabilities.why: NLDAS-2 12 km has no within-cell lapse rate over 2400 m relief.
requires_capabilities.blocks: Clean isolation of the elevation/snow control and accurate ridgetop SWE.

requires_capabilities.why: No in-domain snow observations to validate simulated SWE.

requires_capabilities.capability: model spin-up + WTD-informed warm start execution
requires_capabilities.why: Recharge/drainage and water-table states are targets and cold-start artifacts otherwise.
requires_capabilities.blocks: Trustworthy subsurface partitioning terms for each analysis year.

assumptions: 1993 is representative of a wet year and 2002 of a dry year for this basin over 1980-2018 (from the user request).
Both analysis years use identical column placement and soil so the only deliberate change is the forcing period (paired within-column contrast).
Dominant SSURGO soil classes per elevation band will be resolved by the downstream expander from real rasters; exact classes are not specified here.
A short spin-up window preceding each analysis year is included; exact year spans are set downstream by the configurator.
open_questions: How many USGS gauges fall within HUC 15060103, and is even a simple contributing-area aggregation of column runoff acceptable as a coarse validation?
Should we also report the wet/dry ANOMALY (1993-2002) per column as the primary deliverable rather than absolute annual values?
Is a longer spin-up (multi-year) preferred over the Fan-2013 warm start given the deep default water table in this arid basin?
